name: protect-commit-privacy
description: Keep the development conversation out of git history. Agent-authored commits narrate by default -- who asked for what, which discussion decided it, what the plan was -- and on a public repo that narration is published forever. The guard refuses git commit commands whose message (inline -m/--message or the file behind -F/--file) contains process-leak markers; the rule tells the agent to describe the change, not the conversation, and to propose sensitive messages to the human before committing. Best-effort: markers are a narrow deny-list, and a message the human explicitly approves can say anything -- edit the marker list in the guard, the content is yours. [Session-enforced via a PreToolUse hook; fails open (allows) if python3 or a usable bash is unavailable.]
